title: Event Propagation
body:
Events "bubble up" through it's ancestors by default. ```html (5) then here
(4) then here
(3) then here
    (2) then here
  • (1) Triggers event ``` Which means that *any ancestor* can handle the event. You can change this behavior so that event propagate *downwards*, this is called Capture. Ex: ```html (1) trigger event
    (2) then here
    (3) then here
      (4) then here
    • (5) then here ``` This can be helpful in creating more efficient code: ```html
      • ...
        • ... ... x100 ``` ```js const Lls = document.querySelectorAll("#list li"); for (let li of Lls) { li.addEventListenor("click", () => { ... }) //^ but wait, this will add hundred of these event hadnlers into memory! } ``` Instead of having an event handler in each `li`, we could have a single event handler in the `ul` aka the *parent*. this is called [[Event Delegation]]. **<- IMPORTANT**.
